claims.author: ajtowns
claims.question: What is the intended behavior when txindex is enabled on an already pruned node?
claims.quote: What's the (intended) behaviour if you enable txindex on a node that is already pruned?

status_by.quote: It's the same behavior if you try and start coinstatsindex or blockfilterindex after you've pruned past their last index

claims.status_note: author explained it triggers the same startup error as coinstatsindex or blockfilterindex

claims.author: ajtowns
claims.quote: I'd definitely prefer to have a -prunetxindex=1 option I could set, so that my prune=2000 (~1 week worth of blocks) node could lookup txs without needing to be reprovisioned with extra disk though.
claims.request: add a -prunetxindex=1 option to allow looking up txs without extra disk growth

status_by.quote: I think that could be added as a follow-up, and would not conflict with this approach.

claims.status_note: author replied this could be added as a follow-up

claims.author: mzumsande
claims.quote: However, it would have the big upside that it could be enabled on an already pruned node.
claims.request: Consider a partial index that only indexes non-pruned data so txindex can be enabled on already-pruned nodes

status_by.quote: Partially pruned indexes are out of scope and can be left for a follow-up.

claims.status_note: author removed partial indexing to keep scope smaller and defer to a follow-up

claims.author: arejula27
claims.harm: Return pruned block hashes as structured data rather than inside the error string
claims.quote: Right now those hashes only reach the caller inside the error string, so automating the fetch and retry means parsing the message. Would returning them as structured data be worth it?

status_by.quote: I added returning the pruned block hashes in an optional data field of the JSON error response.

claims.status_note: author returned pruned block hashes in optional data field of JSON error response

claims.author: arejula27
claims.quote: Would a single enum value express that relationship better, so the invariant lives in the type instead of a convention that a future index could break?
claims.request: Use a single enum rather than two separate flags in BaseIndex to express prune policy invariants

status_by.quote: I renamed AllowPrune to GetPrunePolicy which returns an enum.

claims.status_note: author replaced AllowPrune with GetPrunePolicy returning an enum

claims.author: arejula27
claims.quote: Would it make sense to report that hash too?
claims.request: Report the pruned block hash in gettxoutproof when the transaction has unspent outputs

claims.author: arejula27
claims.quote: Would it be worth mentioning that for indexes that allow partial history?
claims.request: Mention deleting the index directory to rebuild partial history from disk when an index falls behind pruned data

status_by.quote: Thanks, but this is no longer relevant since we will not support partial indexes in this change.

claims.status_note: author replied this is no longer relevant after removing partial indexing

claims.author: arejula27
claims.quote: My proposal is to use `std::variant<TxFound, TxMiss>` rather than one struct where the outcome is implied by which fields are set.
claims.request: Use std::variant<TxFound, TxMiss> rather than one struct to ensure consistent fields

claims.author: arejula27
claims.quote: I would add two more scenarios, as I have tested them and they are not covered
claims.request: Add test coverage for pruned blocks outside active chain and returning multiple candidate pruned block hashes
claims.status_note: author added the requested test cases

claims.author: arejula27
claims.question: Whether result can be returned directly instead of reconstructing the object
claims.quote: Is there a reason not to `return result;` directly?

status_by.quote: Removed this, but also it seems no longer relevant since we will not support partial indexes in this change.

claims.status_note: author removed this code and noted it was no longer relevant without partial indexing

claims.author: arejula27
claims.quote: Maybe use a neutral base message here too when the partial history detail is appended, e.g. "Transaction not found"?
claims.request: Use a neutral base error message like 'Transaction not found' when appending partial history details in gettxoutproof

status_by.quote: Thanks, but this is no longer relevant since we will not support partial indexes in this change.

claims.status_note: author replied this is no longer relevant after removing partial indexing

claims.author: fjahr
claims.quote: Would you mind splitting the PR into enabling plain prune mode and keep the partial index and all the related refactorings for a follow-up to that?
claims.request: Split the PR into enabling plain prune mode first and keep partial indexing for a follow-up

status_by.quote: I have updated this to remove the partial index, so this can only work if synced from genesis. Partially pruned indexes

claims.status_note: author removed partial indexing from the PR to leave for a follow-up

claims.author: fjahr
claims.harm: Changing the semantics of synced: true in getindexinfo may break clients that do not check first_block_height
claims.quote: `synced: true` doesn't really mean the same thing as before. So some clients which are not checking the new `first_block_height` may not get what they think they are getting.

status_by.quote: Thanks, but this is no longer relevant since we will not support partial indexes in this change.

claims.status_note: partial indexing was removed, reverting getindexinfo synced semantics

claims.author: fjahr
claims.quote: Starting with `-prune=XXX -txindex=1` may give you a partial or full txindex depending on if you had the index on before. Possibly the partial index could use an explicit opt-in?
claims.request: Consider requiring an explicit opt-in flag for partial indexing to communicate the behavior clearly to users

status_by.quote: I have updated this to remove the partial index, so this can only work if synced from genesis.

claims.status_note: author removed partial indexing from this PR

claims.author: fjahr
claims.question: Whether all information in TxIndexMissErrorDetails like the synced check can ever be hit given f_txindex_ready
claims.quote: Because of what we do with `f_txindex_ready` above I am not sure all the infos in `TxIndexMissErrorDetails` would ever be relevant or possible to hit

claims.author: optout21
claims.quote: If blocks are pruned, the rebuilt txindex will be pruned. The other option is to also restart block download; that way the txindex will be full. If that's the case, is this worth mentioning as well?
claims.request: Consider mentioning in the message that restarting block download allows rebuilding a full txindex when blocks are pruned
claims.status_note: reviewer acknowledged the original request was mistaken and author addressed an edge case

claims.author: optout21
claims.question: In what cases besides duplicate BIP30 coinbases can a transaction hash be present in the active chain more than once
claims.quote: I just wonder in what cases can a TX hash be present in the active chain more than once? Only duplicate coinbase (BIP30)?
claims.status_note: author explained false positives and duplicate coinbases, which reviewer accepted

claims.author: optout21
claims.quote: I think here we could also return `tx_offset_in_block`; it may be useful in some usage scenarios to pass this to the caller as well.
claims.request: Return tx_offset_in_block to the caller as well

status_by.quote: In conclusion, I'm not able to come up with a concrete use case for this, and you are right, then it's best to leave it.

claims.status_note: reviewer agreed there was no concrete use case and withdrew the suggestion

claims.author: optout21
claims.quote: This struct is used both when a TXID is not found in the index, and when it is found, but the block is not found (pruned). This could be mentioned in a doc comment on the struct.
claims.request: Add doc comment explaining TxMiss is used both when txid is missing and when the block is pruned, and clarify redundant phrasing

status_by.quote: I would've argued for a stronger conceptual distinction between "Not in the index" and the "In the index but in a pruned

claims.status_note: reviewer recognized distinction cannot be made due to prefix false positives

claims.author: optout21
claims.quote: For clarity it would be better to separate 3 cases: found, found in pruned block, and not found at all in the index.
claims.request: Separate the 3 lookup cases (found, found in pruned block, not found) in comments/code for clarity

status_by.quote: Same as above: I would've argued for a stronger conceptual distinction between "Not in the index" and the "In the index

claims.status_note: reviewer recognized distinction cannot be made due to prefix false positives

claims.author: optout21
claims.quote: What about if it exists in a block that was not indexed? More correct would be "in a block that has not been indexed or that has been pruned"
claims.request: Update REST documentation to clarify that a block may not have been indexed or has been pruned
claims.status_note: author adopted the suggested documentation wording

claims.author: optout21
claims.quote: The RPC docs are not updated to explain the new behavior, and how possible block hashes are returned.
claims.request: Update RPC docs to explain the new behavior and returned possible block hashes

claims.author: optout21
claims.quote: This change (esp. because of the RPC changes) may warrant a release note.
claims.request: Add a release note for the RPC changes

claims.author: optout21
claims.quote: This string is not added to `bitcoinstrings.cpp`, while the next one is. May be missing.
claims.request: Add missing translation string to bitcoinstrings.cpp

claims.author: optout21
claims.quote: In those cases the "Transaction may be in pruned block X." message is not correct. This looks like a changed error message, even in some cases independent of txindex. If the change is kept, it should be better documented.
claims.request: Fix or document the changed error message when txindex is not set but blockhash is provided or found in the UTXO set

claims.author: optout21
claims.question: Whether the change affects non-txindex cases when a block downloaded by getblockfrompeer has no undo data and blockhash is provided
claims.quote: I wonder if this change may affect non-txindex cases as well, e.g. when a block has been downloaded by `getblockfrompeer` (block data but no undo), and the blockhash is provided.

claims.author: optout21
claims.quote: Theoretically multiple false positives are possible for the same block, in which case a block hash will be included multiple times. The list could be de-duplicated.
claims.request: De-duplicate candidate block hashes when multiple false positives match the same block

claims.author: arejula27
claims.question: Why gettxoutproof and getrawtransaction return different error messages when given an explicit pruned blockhash
claims.quote: With an explicit blockhash whose block is pruned, `gettxoutproof` now returns `Transaction may be in pruned block <hash>.`, while `getrawtransaction` still returns `Block not available`. Is there a reason to treat these two cases differently?
